literal: Friendship not practicing, having become, goodness devoid of things, even to those who do, courtesy not practicing, becoming, is the lowest.
translation: Even towards those who do not maintain friendship and do things devoid of goodness, failing to show courtesy is the lowest of states.
modern: நட்பு கொள்ளாமல் தீமையானவற்றைச் செய்பவர்களிடமும் நற்பண்பு இல்லாமல் நடந்து கொள்வது மிக இழிவான செயலாகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that true courtesy or noble character (paṇpu) must be unconditional. Even when dealing with people who refuse to be friendly (naṇpāṟṟār) and actively do harmful or unpleasant things (nayamila ceyvārkkum), failing to maintain one's own courtesy (paṇpāṟṟār ātal) is considered the lowest, most ignoble state (kaṭai). A person of high character does not let the bad behavior of others dictate their own virtues. Thus, maintaining courtesy is paramount, regardless of how hostile or unjust the other party may be.
